title: Louisiana and Jackson Avenues
summary: He played a trio job there and recalls Creole Fiesta work.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: No, well I played with a little trio over there at Robinson and Houston Avenue for a while there. Well I had oil on piano and I had a boy playing drums, I can't think of his name. You're on my lap, huh? Yeah I had oil on piano and I had another boy sing, play a great trumpet. No he sang, he played a drum. I got in with Celestan too when he went to Delco Island, I can't think of his name. But I know all those guys.
Well I'll call you later about it, I'll phone you up and you can phone me. Anyway, what about other streets like Jackson Avenue, is much happening there?

No, you see after the dewdrops started, Buddy Charles went in there with him and Mr. Kimball and a couple of more places, and the Robin Hood started, that was Paul Gaten, you understand? Paul Gaten started with a trio over there, you understand? And then things just as a standstill with, you know, those group combos, out of town attraction, nothing else happened. Well I was swinging with my band, everywhere. I was playing Creole Fiesta, you know, in different, out of the lake and down in Beerus, you understand? All those oranges grow all down in there. And then alternating in between the time I worked with Willie Pazio and Harold Dejon.
